mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in the past two months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the past month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in the past two months signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k jobs for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 2%, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 5% and 0.3% respectively in the past two months signals a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST increases, UNRATE decreases, and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month, coupled with a CPI (CPIAUCSL) increase of more than 0.5% in the same period, signals stagflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between INDPRO decreases, CPIAUCSL increases, and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
